title: Discovery of the Cell
subject: Biology
objective: In 1665 a thin slice of cork showed tiny boxes Robert Hooke called cells. Then came living cells (1674) and the nucleus (1831).

fill.q: In 1665 Robert Hooke observed thin slices of ____.
Hooke named the boxes "cells" from the Latin word cella, meaning a small ____.
In 1674, ____ saw the first living cells in pond water.

tf.explain: Cork cells are dead; he saw only the walls.
He saw free-living cells in pond water.

tf.q: The nucleus was discovered before the cell.
tf.explain: The cell (1665) came first; the nucleus in 1831.

tf.q: The word "cell" came from the honeycomb-like boxes in cork.

ar.a: Hooke saw only cell walls in cork.
ar.r: Cork is made of dead cells.
ar.explain: Dead cells keep only their walls; R explains A.

ar.r: Leeuwenhoek observed living cells in pond water.
ar.explain: A is false (Robert Brown did, 1831); R is true.

short.q: Why did Hooke see empty boxes in cork?
short.solution: Cork is made of dead cells. Their living contents were gone, leaving only the cell walls.

short.q: Arrange in order with years: nucleus, cork cells, living cells.
